SAP’s Competitive AI Advantage: The Knowledge Graph

Context-aware AI is the next step for business AI. Here’s how the SAP Knowledge Graph powers Joule Work Desktop, EKX, and Joule — and what PMMs should actually use.

October 15, 2026 5 min read

Adapted for Future of PMM from Stefanie Glenk’s SAP News article (Oct 15, 2026). Source

As AI expands across enterprise work, context-aware AI becomes the differentiator. Meaningful results require agents to understand how systems work, how processes run, which APIs matter, and how technical and business knowledge relate.

At SAP, that related knowledge is modeled in a knowledge graph. The company has now consolidated prior enterprise and business knowledge graph efforts into one SAP Knowledge Graph — a shared foundation behind Joule Work Desktop, EKX, Joule, and a growing set of SAP AI services.

Strategically, that gives SAP a unified foundation and one team behind a capability central to the company’s AI ambitions. For PMMs, the shift clarifies why EKX, Joule Work Desktop, and Joule are parts of the same story: making SAP’s AI offerings aware of the knowledge, systems, and processes that define the business.

Primer

What is a knowledge graph?

A knowledge graph turns data into machine-interpretable knowledge by modeling relationships between objects as a network of connected points — not just rows in a table. That structure is what lets AI answer in business language and still stay grounded in how SAP systems actually connect.

  • Integration — connect disparate sources into one queryable view of processes, APIs, configuration, and context.
  • Scale — graphs grow as new sources are added without forcing a rewrite of how you ask questions.
  • Business context — semantic linking helps AI return answers humans can trust and explain.

Why PMMs should care

Generic LLMs guess. The Knowledge Graph is SAP’s content layer for reasoning — so EKX and Joule answers can reflect real product, process, and API relationships instead of plausible fiction. New to the concept? Read the companion primer: Three Things To Know About Knowledge Graphs.

Why this matters for PMMs

One platform, three ways to work

How you consume the graph is less about competing tools and more about intent in the moment. Jan Portisch, head of Knowledge Graph within AI Engineering at SAP, describes it as a stack with the Knowledge Graph as the shared platform — and called this release “the largest update to date for both the SAP Knowledge Graph and EKX.”

  • EKX — web experience for knowledge exploration; creating dashboards, pages, and knowledge apps; plus technical graph work.
  • Joule Work Desktop — everyday productivity workspace for meetings, editorial support, and general or graph-based Q&A via MCP (a standard that lets AI models connect to external tools and data).
  • Joule — transactional assistant embedded in SAP applications, using context to determine which API to call.

PMM takeaway

Use EKX when you need SAP-accurate facts and shareable knowledge assets. Use Joule Work Desktop for day-to-day drafting and research at your desk. Use Joule when you’re already inside an SAP app and need action, not exploration.

AI reasoning and context

A billion triples — and a real user base

At SAP, the Knowledge Graph is the content layer AI systems reason over. “The key differentiator of graphs is integration—and building bridges between process and technical domains, APIs, configuration, business rules, and contextual knowledge,” Jan said.

The graph connects data, apps, and agents with the underlying SAP Business AI Platform — the trusted foundation for autonomous AI.

With the latest consolidation, the graph contains more than one billion reference-knowledge triples across 43 sources. Fourteen new sources were added in the latest release, including the SAP API Hub, SAP Unified Metadata Service, and the SAP Signavio Company Memory.

Beyond Joule and Joule Work Desktop, services drawing on the graph for reasoning and context now include Joule Studio, SAP Cloud ALM (CALM), Joule for Consultants (J4C), and SAP Signavio.

EKX has grown far beyond its early pilot of ~1,500 users: 80,000 SAP employees have accessed it, with 55,000 active in the past 90 days, and about one million requests per month. Roughly 10% of conversations happen on mobile.

“People create to share,” Jan noted — which drove EKX Pages: structured web experiences connected to live APIs that reflect data changes instantly.

New for builders and marketers

Knowledge apps and custom graphs

The October EKX release introduced knowledge apps: reusable packages that combine graph knowledge with external APIs (GitHub, Microsoft tools, and more). Users can keep apps private, share with a group, or submit them to a marketplace that launched with about 20 curated apps.

Sophia Hammes, EKX developer, framed these as a way to stop re-prompting the same recurring tasks — package instructions, context, and system connections once, then reuse.

The team also opened EKX to technical workflows after 200+ requests for knowledge-aware code generation and realistic sample data for simulations.

Separately, the SAP Knowledge Graph foundation offering lets teams assemble custom graphs from selected sources on SAP BTP and expose them through APIs, chat, search, and SPARQL — useful when authorization, governance, or relevance requires a narrower slice of SAP knowledge.

Roadmap

From SAP knowledge to customer knowledge

The current release opens the graph to more users and applications inside SAP. The 2027 direction goes further: an SAP-managed customer knowledge graph that understands not only standard SAP knowledge, but a customer’s actual environment — system versions, modified or disabled APIs, and local ontologies.

“The number-one question we get from customers is to be able to edit the context of the SAP Knowledge Graph and to reference their own data,” Jan said. The roadmap advances content, supports Joule and 200+ SAP applications, and builds a stronger knowledge platform for internal and external customers.

How to act on this in the AI Tools guide

Start with EKX for SAP-accurate competitive and product facts. Add Joule Work Desktop to your daily starter stack. Treat generic LLMs as drafting partners — not as the source of truth for SAP product, process, or API claims.
